title: A finite clopen partition of the base forces vanishing of a discrete defect
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T,S$ be compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological spaces, let $q:T\to S$ be continuous, let $r\geq1$ be an integer, and let $M$ be a finite abelian group with the discrete topology. Give $T^r$ the product topology and write $P_r=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r:q(t_i)=q(t_j)\text{ for all }i,j\}$. Suppose $e:T^r\to M$ is continuous and $e|_{P_r}=0$. A finite clopen partition is a finite collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets with union the whole space; the partition of the empty space is empty. There exists a finite clopen partition $\gamma$ of $S$ such that, for every $B\in\gamma$ and every $(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r$ with $q(t_i)\in B$ for all $i$, one has $e(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})=0$. No surjectivity of $q$ is assumed. Empty spaces and the zero group are allowed.

proof.text: Put $K=e^{-1}(M\setminus\{0\})\subseteq T^r$. Since $M$ is discrete, $M\setminus\{0\}$ is closed, and continuity makes $K$ closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact], $T^r$ is compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact], $K$, with its subspace topology, is compact. The hypothesis $e|_{P_r}=0$ says $K\cap P_r=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tags 08ZU (theorem-tychonov) and 005C (lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact); agent application to the nonzero locus.

proof.text:
For each $x\in K$ there are $i_x,j_x<r$ with $q(x_{i_x})
e q(x_{j_x})$. By Hausdorffness choose disjoint open neighbourhoods $U,V$ of these two points. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] to obtain clopen $C_x\subseteq U$ containing $q(x_{i_x})$; then $q(x_{j_x})
otin C_x$. The set $W_x=\{t\in T^r:q(t_{i_x})\in C_x,\ q(t_{j_x})
otin C_x\}$ is open: it is the intersection of the inverse images of the open sets $C_x$ and $S\setminus C_x$ under the continuous coordinate maps $q\circ\mathrm{pr}_{i_x}$ and $q\circ\mathrm{pr}_{j_x}$. It contains $x$. The sets $W_x\cap K$ therefore cover the compact subspace $K$. Its defining open-cover property gives a finite set $A\subseteq K$ with $K\subseteq igcup_{a\in A}W_a$; retain their data $i_a,j_a,C_a$. Each $W_a$ is disjoint from $P_r$: its two displayed coordinate images lie on opposite sides of $C_a$ and hence are unequal. If $K$ is empty take $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), clopen basis consequence; agent compact-cover construction.

proof.text: For each function $\epsilon:A\to\{0,1\}$ form $B_\epsilon=\bigcap_{\epsilon(a)=1}C_a\cap\bigcap_{\epsilon(a)=0}(S\setminus C_a)$, taking an empty intersection to be $S$. Let $\gamma$ be the collection of nonempty $B_\epsilon$. It is finite, and every block is clopen by finite intersections and complements. A point $s\in S$ belongs precisely to the block whose membership pattern is $\epsilon(a)=1\iff s\in C_a$. Distinct patterns give disjoint blocks. Hence $\gamma$ is a finite clopen partition, empty when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Agent finite Boolean refinement of the clopens, as in the partition construction in Tag 08ZY (lemma-profinite).

proof.text:
Let $B\in\gamma$ and suppose all $q(t_i)$ belong to $B$. If $e(t)
e0$, then $t\in K$, so some selected $W_a$ contains $t$. This gives $q(t_{i_a})\in C_a$ and $q(t_{j_a})
otin C_a$. But the block $B$ lies either in $C_a$ or in its complement, a contradiction. Thus $e(t)=0$. No point of $S$ was lifted along $q$. For $r=1$ every tuple belongs to $P_r$, so $K=\varnothing$; likewise $M=0$ or $T=\varnothing$ gives $K=\varnothing$. When $A=\varnothing$ the construction yields $\{S\}$ if $S
e\varnothing$ and the empty partition otherwise.
